title: Commodity Prices Swing as Gold Rebounds 2.75%
summary: Spot gold rose 2.75% Monday as stocks recovered, copper briefly broke below $12,000 a ton, and oil and European gas swung. Here is what drove each move.
body_markdown:
## Copper Dips Below $12,000 on AI Spending Doubts


Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange fell to around $11,958.93 a ton in early Monday trading, its weakest level since March, before recovering to $12,240.50 by 03:40 GMT, according to Investing.com. The metal lost about 9% last week as concerns over artificial intelligence spending, a stronger dollar and the prospect of higher interest rates weighed on prices.


Copper hit a record high of $14,694 a ton in September,[The National](https://www.thenationalnews.com/business/markets/2026/11/23/copper-sinks-below-12000-for-the-first-time-since-march-amid-ai-demand-uncertainty/) reported. "Copper fell sharply from September highs amid growing doubts about the scale and returns of AI-related spending," Tony Sage, chief executive of Australia-based Critical Metals, told the publication.


## Oil Swings After Monday's 3.5% Brent Drop


WTI settled down 3.9% at $80.17 a barrel on Monday and Brent declined 3.5% to $89.37, according to Kitco, as Middle East oil flows recovered and a Libyan pipeline restarted. Prices bounced on Tuesday, when Brent settled up $2.03, or 2.27%, at $91.40 and WTI rose $1.88, or 2.35%, to $82.05,[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/24/oil-wti-brent-hormuz-supply.html) reported, as traders weighed continued ship attacks near the Strait of Hormuz.


"Oil prices are facing modest downward pressure from two sides: markets are pricing out some near-term geopolitical risk," UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo said, according to CNBC, naming strategic reserve releases as the other.


## European Gas Rises for a Fourth Session With Storage at 68.9%


European gas prices rose for a fourth straight session on Tuesday, when the Dutch TTF benchmark topped 90.50 euros per megawatt-hour in Amsterdam trade, up about 1%, after soaring by more than 8% at Monday's open,[Oilprice.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/european-gas-prices-climb-cold-114500978.html) reported. EU gas storage sites were only 68.9% full as of November 23, against a five-year average of 89%, according to Gas Infrastructure Europe data cited by the outlet, with freezing temperatures forecast this week in the UK, Germany and France.


## How Does a Gold ETF Differ From Owning Physical Gold?


A gold ETF investor owns fund shares rather than bars, and State Street Global Advisors says the value of GLD shares relates directly to the value of the gold the trust holds, less its expenses. GLD's stated objective is for its shares to reflect the performance of the price of gold bullion, less the fund's expenses, and its benchmark is the LBMA Gold Price PM.
